newsitem.title: USA: U.S. not worried about Russian deal with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. not worried about Russian deal with Iraq.

text.p: A U.S. official Friday said there was no reason to question Russia's commitment to U.N. sanctions against Iraq despite the signing of a contract by Russia to develop Iraq's Qurana oilfield.
"They haven't (violated sanctions) up to now. There's no reason to think they would now," the administration official told Reuters.
Russia and Iraq signed a deal earlier Friday to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in the Qurana oil field in southern Iraq.
Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said the contract would be carried out regardless of United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.

The U.S. official said the Clinton administration did not have enough information yet to stake out a position on the contract. But "the seriousness with which Russia has abided by sanctions gives us no reason to question their commitment, based on a press article," he said, referring to reports of the deal.
He said this contract could be similar to other "executory contracts" that have been signed with Iraq, which are contingent on the lifting of sanctions.
The United Nations has declined to comment on the Russian contract so far.
